pr.title: Improve managed hosting and self-hosted administration
pr.body:
## Summary
- Make managed Calibrate hosting the default end-user path, with an explicit, tested, cancelable self-hosted chooser
- Move account/service identity into Service & hosting, separate from app diagnostics and updates
- Add a server administration overview, capabilities, searchable/paginated user directory, and confirmed admin/member changes
- Persist server roles with atomic first-account ownership for new self-hosted databases; managed hosting never grants the first public registrant administrator access
- Import existing valid ADMIN_USER_IDS once, protect the last verified administrator, and provide an explicit recovery command for an existing verified account
- Isolate credentials, password recovery, in-flight refreshes, and admin mutations across account/server changes

## Verification
- Final head a341dcf2e736c8207c7e9296c1c7a8f67cf012f5 passed all six PR workflows: [Builds and browser smoke](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903424), [Tests](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903373), [Lint](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903442), [Database upgrade/rollback](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903405), [Dependency audit](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903488), and [Production container scan](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36914903426)
- 1,083 mobile tests passed (214 suites)
- 717 backend tests passed with test-concurrency=2; an initial unconstrained run had one governance-file failure that passed in isolation and in the complete rerun
- 73 API-client tests passed
- Full lint/typechecks, backend production build, and Expo web production build passed
- Web-release checks, release configuration checks, rollback ledger checks (14), and populated-upgrade unit checks (3) passed
- OpenAPI regeneration is byte-identical to the committed generated client
- Independent security review and re-review found no remaining blocking issue

## Rollout notes
- Migration 0042 stores admin/member roles and one-time bootstrap/import state
- CALIBRATE_HOSTED_SERVICE=true disables first-user ownership regardless of NODE_ENV
- Existing populated installations do not promote a new registrant automatically
- Existing zero-admin installations use the documented operator recovery command against an existing verified account
- No production access changes, merge, or deployment have been performed

## Screenshot evidence
[Full paired gallery: all 14 unedited PNGs](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/a341dcf2e736c8207c7e9296c1c7a8f67cf012f5/docs/pr-screenshots/self-hosting/README.md) · [Provenance and image hashes](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/a341dcf2e736c8207c7e9296c1c7a8f67cf012f5/docs/pr-screenshots/self-hosting/manifest.json) · [Original CI artifact](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/36913482326/artifacts/11188925700)

Captured from code commit df7e610812408e59a1e340dd8f32ab94fe4b4289. Real Chromium, synthetic intercepted API fixtures, no customer data or live role changes. The browser job passed 24 tests with no retries; every capture was visually inspected. These are web viewport screenshots, not native-device evidence. The subsequent gallery commit changes only documentation/images.

## Validation limits
- Populated PostgreSQL upgrade and encrypted rollback passed in CI; dedicated live cross-connection RBAC concurrency remains unverified
- Real phone/desktop browser evidence passed in CI; local browser and native-device QA remain unavailable
- Native-only server selection is covered by component tests; browser captures will not be presented as native-device evidence

The initially published product tree is exactly the locally reviewed tree 4e6426ce765a37b54ec87d4c8faff3a962f366d0 (local review commit 89b616b; GitHub commit ec041fefe76d49eed0aefdd0bcf725548bb8e8f0).

inline.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move directory scans outside the exclusive ownership lock**

On a populated managed instance, every `/server-settings/users` request holds the singleton `ServerAccessState` row's exclusive `FOR UPDATE` lock for the entire directory query. The case-insensitive substring search can scan the `User` table, and registrations, role changes, feature updates, and account deletions all need the same lock, so one slow search blocks those operations and concurrent directory reads unnecessarily serialize. Keep the ownership lock limited to authorization/ownership mutations, or provide an indexed access path that does not hold this exclusive lock while listing users.
